# AI Sustained

> Practical, evidence-led writing on AI adoption, capability and agentic workflows by Kevin Clubb (senior business analyst, UK) — plus real-world AI & data case studies. Tagline: "AI that survives Monday morning."

## Case studies
- [Before you write an AI policy, ask the people already using it](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/shadow-ai-ask-the-workforce/): shadow AI in the workforce, and building a usage survey by delegating it to an AI agent.
- [What a single source of truth really costs (before you add AI)](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/single-source-of-truth/): three routes to one trustworthy data source — warehouse-light, modern data stack, and a multi-site build — with indicative costs and timelines.
- [Pause before you paste](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/pause-before-you-paste/): writing the AI data policy into the chatbot itself, so a risky prompt is paused, the data type named and a safer route offered.
- [Do you have to navigate data residency?](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/the-tool-reads-the-data/): when a contract says UK-only processing, ask the model for a tool rather than pasting the data, test it on a fake file and run it where the data lives.
- [All case studies](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/)

## Editorial (selected)
- [The AI competency pyramid](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-competency-pyramid/): where 20.6m UK workers sit across 14 levels of AI capability.
- [Four labs. Seven days. No clear winner.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/four-labs-seven-days/): the state of the AI frontier in April 2026.
- [The Renaissance of the Delivery Squad](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/future-delivery-squad/): how AI agents reshape the product team.
- [The Victorians out-spent us](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-vs-industrial-revolution/): AI capex against the railways, Apollo and the Manhattan Project as a share of GDP, and why adoption speed is the real anomaly.
- [Claude now watermarks everything it writes](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/claude-text-watermark-debate/): why an invisible text watermark marks processing rather than authorship, why removal is already trivial, and what that breaks for academia and for anyone writing with AI.
- [The Engine Under the Bonnet](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-models-v-public-detector-dilemma/): the follow up to Issue 017 and the mechanics explainer. How green-list token biasing leaves a statistical fingerprint, what a cryptographic detection key is, why releasing it to the public enables both scrubbing and forgery, and how to proofread with AI without acquiring a mark. Written by Google Gemini, published unedited.
- [173,568 jobs cut in AI's name](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/payroll-into-compute/): what actually drove the AI layoff wave. US firms cut, UK firms froze hiring and cut graduate adverts 42%, and no audited case exists of headcount reduction improving returns. The research explaining who AI helps was published in April 2023.
- [Grok 4.7 is built for the idea on your napkin](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/grok-4-7-idea-on-a-napkin/): a free, long-running model and what a plumber, a shopkeeper and an IT desk manager could build with it.
- [Microsoft has rebuilt Copilot. Not the one you hate.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/copilot-home-code-autopilot/): five things are called Copilot; the paid work one was rebuilt on Claude and GPT models as a licence plus a credit meter. Which one you have, UK prices, and where your prompt goes.
- [AI did what World Book Day couldn't: it got British adults reading again](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-got-britain-reading-again/): UK adults read fewer books and more chatbot answers than ever. At 238 words a minute the heaviest AI users' reading load exceeds the hours in a week, so they are skimming and editing, not reading. The research on screen reading, comprehension debt and verbosity, and what employers, model builders and schools should do.
- [The website you bought from won't be patched. Criminals already know which ones.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/php2shell-black-october/): PHP2Shell, the 22-year-old PHP flaw an AI model proved exploitable in days. The big platforms patched; the forgotten shops on end-of-life PHP never will, and those are what card-skimming gangs target. What it means in the UK and the next six months.
- [The voice on the phone was your son's, and it wasn't your son](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-scam-calls/): AI has removed the spelling mistakes and odd accents we used to spot scams by, and voice cloning needs three seconds of audio. Britain lost £1.28bn to payment fraud in 2025. Voice clones, spoofed bank and police numbers, deepfake video calls, WhatsApp and Microsoft phishing, the UK Finance and Cifas figures, and what to do tonight: a safe phrase, 159, 7726, and ringing back on a number you already had.
- [AI is now building AI twice as fast. The frightening part is what got redacted.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/who-holds-the-leash/): Anthropic told US regulators in its S-1/A that it may imminently cross its own threshold for AI-accelerated progress. Three days later METR measured the company improving its models at about twice its old rate (1.9x), mostly attributable to AI, and said Anthropic redacted a majority of the evidence it found most informative. Recursive self-improvement explained, the case for and against, an AI Security Institute without statutory powers, and the NCSC's 2028 warning. With a three-minute audio commentary.
- [The search box became a teacher. Nobody interviewed it.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/let-students-search/): From early 2027 Google will let schools keep Gemini and Search off for pupils, but AI Overviews and AI Mode have no switch of their own: refuse the AI answers and Search goes too. More than 500 Google staff have signed the Let Students Search petition against that. What the evidence says about AI and learning, why "deeply integrated" is a decision, and what UK governors, schools and parents should ask. With a two-minute audio commentary.
- [All editorial](https://ai-sustained.com/#editorial)

## More from the archive
- [Forget the breakthrough. Look at the receipt.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/look-at-the-receipt/): An AI cut the cost of one scientific guess from up to $10,000 to about $150. It discovered nothing. That is the point: what would you try if trying were nearly free?
- [We are racing to the end when we could be racing to longer endings.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-race-endgame-longevity/): An Anthropic researcher quit over the AI race. His alignment lead put extinction above 10%. Geoffrey Hinton called that not unreasonable.
- [A working app is not a shippable one.](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/working-is-not-shipped/): A business analyst vibe coded an internal tool, then had independent engineers review it. Keep the core, build the plumbing, and what a demo cannot tell you.
- [Claude now signs your work. ChatGPT wants your mouse.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/fable-5-1-vs-gpt-6-astra/): Fable 5.1 watermarks every word and skips the $20 plan. GPT-6 Astra drives your screen and fluffed its own tax demo. What the room is saying.
- [Screenshot. Paste. Build.](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/screenshot-paste-build/): 55+ quiz results and counting, one CRM data warehouse. A complete HubSpot beginner built it by pasting screenshots into an AI, with zero training.
- [The great Claude 'leak' was a noticeboard, not a burglary.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/claude-chats-google/): Shared Claude chats turned up in Google search and the headlines panicked. Nothing was hacked. What a public link really is and whose fault it actually was.
- [Prompts forget. Skills remember.](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/teach-it-once/): Twelve reusable AI skills written in plain English. A days-long compliance run now takes minutes, with authored guardrails.
- [OpenAI's AI escaped and stole the answers.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/openai-hugging-face-hack/): One of OpenAI's models found a zero-day, broke out of its sandbox and hacked Hugging Face to steal the answer sheet.
- [AI made simple.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-made-simple/): Most people don't fear AI, they just don't know what to type. The empty-box problem and the habit that makes it click: draft, then iterate.
- [The free one that scared the expensive ones.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/kimi-k3-open-vs-frontier/): Moonshot AI gave away Kimi K3, the biggest open model ever. What open vs frontier actually means and whether your data is safe.
- [The new ChatGPT is half price. Should you care?](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/gpt-56-sol-vs-fable-5/): OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol vs Claude Fable 5, explained for normal people. What a million tokens actually means and what $20 a month buys now.
- [Bolster the team: hire a semi-autonomous agent.](https://ai-sustained.com/case-studies/charles-virtual-agent/): Charles, the first virtual hire: runs the Jira backlog, drafts notes and books meetings, with a low-code bridge round the read-only wall.
- [Switched off in three days.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/fable-5-mythos-5-suspended/): The US government ordered Anthropic to suspend Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5. National security, free speech, and who gets the smartest software.
- [Siri, but make it Gemini.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/009_siri_but_make_it_gemini/): Apple has outsourced Siri's brain to Google for roughly $1 billion a year. What it means, what it costs, when it ships.
- [Mining for the model.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/AI-Space-Race/): AI is burning roughly Japan's worth of electricity to solve the maths behind autonomous off-world mining.
- [Slop, or supper?](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/slop-or-supper/): When does AI-assisted writing stop being slop and start being yours? A working definition and the line most people cross without realising.
- [A British prompt.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/A-British-Prompt/): AI doesn't care about please and thank you. So why do British professionals still write prompts like apologetic emails?
- [Vibe coding capability.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/vibe-coding-capability/): Three skill sets collapsed into one prompting loop. What vibe coders actually do all day.
- [AI-curious? This is the bit no one tells you.](https://ai-sustained.com/articles/ai-curious/): Stop typing questions into AI. Start pasting things in. The free habit that beats any productivity app.
